title: ACLU test finds Amazon Rekognition falsely matched 28 members of Congress to mugshots
description: On 26 July 2018, the ACLU of Northern California published results of a test in which it used Amazon's Rekognition facial-recognition software, at default match settings, to compare photos of all then-current members of Congress against a database of roughly 25,000 public arrest photos. The test produced 28 false matches, with people of colour disproportionately misidentified — nearly 40% of false matches, against roughly 20% representation in Congress, including six members of the Congressional Black Caucus. The findings contributed to years of subsequent scrutiny, including San Francisco's May 2019 ordinance banning government facial-recognition use — the first such ban by a major US city — and Amazon's own June 2020 moratorium on police use of Rekognition, extended indefinitely in May 2021.

history.note: Initial Edition 1.1 content, part of the Phase 3 canonical expansion. Amazon disputed the ACLU's methodology at the time (arguing the ACLU used an 80% confidence threshold rather than the 95%+ threshold Amazon recommends for law-enforcement use); neither the SF ordinance nor Amazon's 2020 moratorium cites this test as their sole cause — both followed broader activism and the 2020 protests as more proximate triggers.

root_cause: The ACLU attributed the false-match rate to limitations and bias in the facial-recognition algorithm as configured with default (lower-confidence) match settings, compounded by broader documented tendencies of facial-recognition systems to perform less accurately on darker-skinned individuals.

citations.title: Amazon's Face Recognition Falsely Matched 28 Members of Congress With Mugshots

relationships.reason: A requirement for independent public accuracy testing before law-enforcement procurement directly addresses the gap this test exposed.
This incident belongs to the same biometric consent-and-accuracy governance concept already established by the Rite Aid and Clearview AI cases.
